newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai passes order to set up free trade zone.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai passes order to set up free trade zone.

text.p: Shanghai's city legislature passed regulations on Thursday to provide a legal basis for China's largest free trade zone, the Xinhua news agency said.

The regulations, which take effect from January 1, allow businesses set up in the Shanghai Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone in the east of China's commercial hub to trade freely with foreign counterparts without quotas or licences and ensure access to current-account convertibility of China's yuan currency.

The new regulations were intended to improve the investment environment of the Pudong New Area, designated by Beijing as China's future financial centre, and to boost the confidence of international businesses based in the zone, Xinhua said.
Passage of the rules provides a legal basis for the management and operation of China's largest free trade zone, set up in 1990 and covering 10 square km, Xinhua said.
Businesses in the zone can trade freely with overseas counterparts without the limitation of quotas and licences, except for items subject to special state rules, the rules say.
Both domestic and overseas businesses can store their goods in the zone with no time limit.

Businesses in the zone will have access to current-account convertibility of the yuan and certain foreign currencies designated by state financial regulatory departments can circulate in the zone, the rules say.
Income taxes for businesses in the zone will be set at 15 percent.
China presently has 15 free trade and bonded zones.
By end-September, 2,672 projects had been approved in the zone, with total investment of $3.27 billion of which $1.593 billion was contracted foreign investment, Xinhua said.

In 1995, the volume of import and export and entrepot trade through the zone reached $940 million US dollars, and the monthly business volume of its bonded trading market exceeded $100 million, it said.
